svg.text: FEEDBACK: SBI + PENDLETON (not the sandwich dodge)

g.text: SBI — Situation (\"on the drug round at 10:00…\") → Behavior (\"…you skipped the allergy check…\")
→ Impact (\"…so a reaction could have been missed — and you looked rushed, are you OK?\").
Pendleton — learner goes FIRST (what went well? what to change?) → preceptor adds → agree ONE
action. Rules: soon, private, specific, behaviour-not-person, balanced, forward-looking, documented.
Difficult learners: diagnose before disciplining — knowledge gap (teach), skills gap
(drill), attitude gap (values talk + consequences), welfare gap (money, health, grief — refer:
counselling, SRC, chaplaincy), unsafe gap (remove from risk NOW, remediate, re-assess).
FAILING honestly (the profession's immune system): warn early + in writing (no surprise
fails) → support plan (objectives, mentor, timeline, evidence) → re-assess fairly → if still
unsafe, FAIL + document + report to school (passing the unsafe endangers hundreds of future
patients — kindness to one student is cruelty to them all). Appeals respected, records kept.
Mentor duties: orient (ward, people, emergencies, expectations), set objectives (3 per
placement, SMART), observe + countersign (PRO-I: students never solo beyond scope),
protect (rest, meals, nights supervised, bullying intercepted), debrief scares same-shift,
assess fairly (evidence, not favouritism — your signature vouches to the NMC).
Role-model rule: students copy your hand hygiene, your tone with cleaners, your honesty
about errors — the hidden curriculum out-teaches every lesson plan. Teach the nurse
you'd trust with your own mother: competent hands, honest mouth, kind eyes.
Exam line: \"feedback feeds forward — specific, soon, private, and always with a next step.\"
